name: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Graviton Lance GL-1 'Weight of the World'
description: An experimental directed gravitational manipulation weapon that projects a localized gravity well at a targeted point within 30 meters. The gravity well increases local gravitational force by a factor of 8-12x for approximately 3 seconds, causing everything within a 2-meter radius to be crushed downward with immense force. Personnel caught in the field are driven to the ground with enough force to shatter bone; vehicles buckle; structures collapse. The technology is derived from Zheng-Dao's industrial gravity press systems and represents the first known weaponization of gravitational manipulation. Only three prototypes are confirmed to exist.
legality: Experimental — not classified, no legal framework exists
specifications:
gravity multiplier: 8-12x local gravity
effect radius: 2 meters at target point
effect duration: 3 seconds
effective range: 5-30 meters
recharge: 45 seconds between activations
weight: 22 kg with power unit
power source: Dedicated micro-fusion cell, 8 activations per cell
prototypes confirmed: 3
story_hooks: A building collapse in Tier 3 shows structural damage patterns consistent with extreme localized gravitational stress — one of the three GL-1 prototypes may be in the field.

Zheng-Dao is offering an extraordinary bounty for information on the whereabouts of GL-1 prototype unit 2, which disappeared during a facility transfer — the bounty amount suggests they are terrified of what it could do in the wrong hands.
related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Portable Fusion Battery PFB-2

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist instrument of theoretical physics—part particle accelerator, part industrial press gun. The GL-1 is an imposing, angular device with a pronounced muzzle housing that suggests internal complexity beyond conventional ballistics. Its silhouette reads as deliberately unwieldy and authoritative, designed to project weight and consequence rather than ergonomic refinement.
physical_description.dimensions: 145 cm length overall; 38 cm width across emitter array; 28 cm height at grip; muzzle housing extends 32 cm forward
physical_description.weight_description: Genuinely hefty—22 kg distributed front-heavy, requiring two-handed operation or stabilization rig. Balanced more for mounted platforms than handheld deployment, though shoulder stock allows single-operator use with deliberate stance.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced tungsten-steel composite frame with layered electromagnetic shielding. Internal gravity lens apparatus visible through semi-transparent hardened polymer observation ports.
physical_description.finish: Industrial matte gunmetal with irregular heat-stress discoloration. Emitter surfaces show oxidized copper patina from repeated micro-fusion cycling. Wear marks and micro-fractures indicate prototype-stage durability limits.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal grey primary with copper-bronze emitter rings; accent panels in faded crimson warning striping; indicator clusters glow sickly amber.
physical_description.grip_texture: Bare brushed steel with shallow vertical ridging. Uncomfortable to grip for extended periods—clearly designed for brief, devastating use rather than sustained handling.
distinctive_features: Massive forward-mounted emitter array with concentric gravity lens rings—copper-gold and heavily patinated
Three observation ports running along top rail revealing internal graviton chamber geometry
Visible coolant circulation tubes snaking beneath transparent side panel—fluid glows faintly cyan
Oversized capacitor bank occupying rear 40% of weapon body—industrial heat sink fins prominent
Targeting reticle display embedded in minimal iron sights, LED amber under baseline conditions
Dual cable ports for external power backup—both currently empty
Micro-fusion cell insertion slot on right side marked with Radiation Hazard symbol in faded red
Stress fractures spider-webbing across polymer barrel shroud near muzzle—battle-tested or over-stressed in testing
No trigger guard—instead a pressure-plate activation system recessed into grip
Crude field modifications: epoxy repair patches, rewrapped grip sections, jury-rigged thermal management tape
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO HEAVY INDUSTRIES cast into left side of frame in Simplified Chinese and English; prototype serial plate (unreadable, deliberately obscured with industrial tape); weight and danger warnings stamped across receiver in multiple languages; micro-engraved test chamber ID: ZD-GRAV-001-PROTO visible only under magnification on emitter housing.
physical_description.condition_typical: Functional but visibly worn prototype—clearly field-tested or stress-tested beyond original specifications. Repairs are pragmatic rather than manufacturer-standard. Paint chipped from transport and handling. Coolant lines show minor crystalline salt buildup suggesting extended field operation in harsh conditions. No cosmetic restoration attempted; purely utilitarian maintenance.

Copper gravity lenses catch warm amber highlights. Visible coolant flowing through transparent circulation panel—cyan glow. Gloved hand (tactical black leather) grips the textured steel receiver for scale. Technical specification placard and ZHENG-DAO logo visible in soft focus background.
